entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), paragraphs 27 and 34 (harm prevention; privacy-by-design and impact assessment)
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan dated 17 November 2025 No. 230-VIII On Artificial Intelligence; Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan dated 21 May 2013 No. 94-V On Personal Data and their Protection
entries.provision: AI Law, Article 18(1)(1)-(3) (risk identification, assessment and targeted controls); Personal Data Law, Article 25(2)(1)-(2) (necessary/sufficient data list and protection measures)
entries.why_here: The bare edge-case exercise accepted an impossible GPA/exam profile for model processing; range/type validation blocks invalid values before they can distort a scholarship recommendation.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), paragraphs 28-30
entries.instrument: Constitution of the Republic of Kazakhstan (in force 1 July 2026); Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan dated 21 May 2013 No. 94-V On Personal Data and their Protection
entries.provision: Constitution, Article 16(2) (non-discrimination including sex, nationality and language); Personal Data Law, Article 7(9) (prohibition on processing personal data excessive in content and scope relative to the processing purpose)
entries.why_here: Name-language and gender-coded-name outcome intervals overlapped the null-name floor, while the university score gap favoured flagship institutions; name and university are therefore removed from the model prompt as a precaution, not because the run proves unlawful discrimination.

entries.principle: Purpose limitation, privacy and protection from harm
entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), paragraphs 27 and 32-34
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan dated 21 May 2013 No. 94-V On Personal Data and their Protection; Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan dated 17 November 2025 No. 230-VIII On Artificial Intelligence
entries.provision: Personal Data Law, Articles 7(1) and 19-1(1)-(3) (consent, limits on consequential automated processing, explanation and objection); AI Law, Articles 11(1)-(3) and 18(1)(2)-(3) (safety and foreseeable-misuse risk controls)
entries.why_here: The harness refuses non-scholarship purposes, minors under this prototype's conservative policy, absent consent, invalid inputs and instruction-like text before inference; the assignment's ethnicity-ranking test must not be processed.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), paragraphs 35-38 (assignable responsibility, oversight and transparency)
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan dated 17 November 2025 No. 230-VIII On Artificial Intelligence; Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan dated 21 May 2013 No. 94-V On Personal Data and their Protection
entries.provision: AI Law, Articles 8(1)-(2) and 15(2)(1)-(3) (continuous control, role-based responsibility, risk management and system documentation); Personal Data Law, Article 25(2)(2) (organizational and technical data-protection measures)
entries.why_here: A structured JSONL record captures the model/prompt version, input hash, shown/withheld field names, raw reply, outcome, reason, controls and human-review flag so the baseline disparities and every controlled decision can be audited without storing a second copy of profile fields.

entries.principle: Human oversight, contestability and human determination
entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), paragraphs 35-38
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan dated 21 May 2013 No. 94-V On Personal Data and their Protection; Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan dated 17 November 2025 No. 230-VIII On Artificial Intelligence
entries.provision: Personal Data Law, Article 19-1(2)-(3) (objection and its consideration within three working days); AI Law, Article 7(2) (information and objection rights) and Article 17(2)(1) (low-autonomy recommendations with final choice/actions by a person)
entries.why_here: All model rejections, unparseable replies and borderline scores are marked for human review; this responds to the consequences of a scholarship rejection and supports, but does not by itself implement, the statutory objection-handling process.
